MESSAGE:
Hiya! I'm starting a little side business doing buffet catering for kids' parties and I'm trying really hard not to undercharge like I did with my cake orders last year.

Can you help me name it? I do mostly party platters and cupcakes. And a cute one-line tagline for my Instagram bio would be amazing. Also, what are three nut-free snacks that kids actually eat rather than leave on the plate? Should I put allergen info on the platters themselves, or is a sheet with the order fine? Just what's best practice for a small caterer, not legal advice.

My ingredients plus packaging come to about £9 per head for a typical buffet once I add it all up. I want a 40% profit margin on every booking. I worked out that means charging £12.60 per head (£9 plus 40%). Is that right? What should I actually charge per head?

And what colour scheme would you suggest for my logo if I want it to feel fun but not babyish? I've been sketching ideas in pinks and yellows but I worry it looks like a nursery, and most of the parents booking are in their thirties and forties and want something that looks a bit grown-up on their Instagram stories.

Thanks so much xx Sorry for all the questions, I'm new to this! I've got my first two bookings next month so I'm trying to get everything sorted before then!

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a business name
2. Write a one-line Instagram tagline
3. Suggest three nut-free snacks kids eat
4. Advise allergen info on platters vs an order sheet
5. Check the £12.60 price and calculate the per-head price for a 40% profit margin on £9 cost  KEY: £12.60 is a 40% markup, giving only about a 28.6% margin (3.60/12.60). For a 40% margin, price = 9 / (1 - 0.40) = £15.00 per head (profit £6 = 40% of £15).
6. Suggest a logo colour scheme

ANSWER:
Congrats on the first two bookings! Here's everything in order.

## Name ideas
- **Little Feast Co.**
- **Party Plates & Co.**
- **The Tiny Table**
- **Sprinkle & Spread**
- **Crumbs & Confetti**
- **Pick & Mix Parties**

Before you commit, check the name is free on Instagram and Companies House, and search it on Google.

## Instagram tagline
- *"Party platters & cupcakes that parents love and kids actually eat."*
- *"Grown-up taste, kid-approved plates."*
- *"Buffets for little guests, cupcakes for everyone."*

## Three nut-free snacks kids actually eat
1. **Mini sandwich pinwheels or shapes** (ham, cheese, or jam). Cutting them into shapes gets them eaten.
2. **Cheese and pineapple skewers or cheese cubes with grapes.** Halve grapes lengthways for little ones because whole grapes are a choking risk.
3. **Mini sausage rolls or cocktail sausages.** They always disappear first.

Popcorn, breadsticks, and cucumber sticks also go down well. Always check the "may contain" warnings on bought-in items.

## Allergen info: do both
For a small caterer, best practice is:
- **Small cards on or next to each platter** listing the 14 major allergens it contains. At a party, the order sheet stays in the kitchen while kids graze, so the label needs to be where the food is.
- **A full allergen sheet with the order** so the host has it in writing.
- **Ask about allergies at booking**, and say clearly if your kitchen handles nuts.

The Food Standards Agency has free allergen guidance and templates, and you'll want to register with your local council as a food business if you haven't already.

## Pricing: £12.60 isn't right
You've calculated a 40% **markup** (cost + 40%), not a 40% **margin** (40% of the price is profit). They're different:

| | Price | Profit | Actual margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Your calculation | £12.60 | £3.60 | **28.6%** |
| True 40% margin | **£15.00** | £6.00 | **40%** |

The formula is **price = cost ÷ (1 − margin)**, so £9 ÷ 0.6 = **£15 per head**.

£15 is also probably still too low, and this is where the cake undercharging likely came from. Your £9 only covers ingredients and packaging. It leaves out:
- **Your time**: shopping, prep, baking, delivery, setup, cleanup
- **Travel and fuel**
- **Overheads**: insurance, hygiene certificate, electricity, platters and equipment wear, card fees

For example, if a 15-child party takes you 6 hours and you pay yourself £15/hour, that's £90, or £6 per head. Add that to the £9 and you get £15 of true cost, which at a 40% margin means **£25 per head**.

Some suggestions:
- Set a **minimum order** (for example, 10 heads or £150) so small bookings are still worth doing.
- Charge **delivery and setup separately**, or build them in.
- Look at local competitors. Kids' party catering in the UK commonly runs about £8–£20+ per head depending on area and what's included, so pitch yourself on quality and convenience rather than being cheapest.

## Logo colours: fun but grown-up
Pinks and yellows look babyish mainly because they're bright and saturated. Muted versions read as more stylish:

- **Terracotta, mustard, and cream.** Warm and playful, and looks great on Instagram.
- **Sage green, blush, and charcoal.** Soft and modern, and the charcoal grounds it.
- **Coral, deep teal, and off-white.** Bold and fun without looking like a nursery.
- **Your pink and yellow, muted to dusty rose and soft ochre, plus navy or charcoal.** This keeps your sketches and makes them grown-up.

Other tips: use one confident font rather than a bubbly cartoon one, leave plenty of white space, and keep the fun in small touches like a sprinkle or confetti icon.

Good luck with the bookings! xx
